probes.question: Where did waste water from Mohenjo-daro's houses go?
options: Into covered drains along the streets

probes.question: True or false: Mohenjo-daro had roughly one well for every three houses.

image.alt: Excavated brick ruins of Mohenjo-daro with the Great Bath in the foreground and a stupa on the mound behind

body.question: Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley, was planned with water supply and drainage built in from the start. About how many wells have been found there so far?
body.reveal: Over 700 wells, about one for every three houses. Waste water was carried by a centralized drainage system, in covered drains along the streets. The Indus civilisation is credited with the world's first known city sanitation systems.
